#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""nuxel_live — capability-based access to the *running* Nuxel S10+ over its
USB CDC-ACM "Live Console", plus the guards that keep live work flash-free.

WHY THIS MODULE EXISTS (briq-10a/10b/10c, Priority 9 "Live S10+ Deployment")
==========================================================================
The live-phone build group is the only group allowed to touch the physical
device, and it must do so *safely and identically every time*:

  * the console tty node must be found **by capability** (USB VID/PID + the
    gadget's TTY base/suffix + serial), never by a hard-coded node name such as
    ``/dev/cu.usbmodem201`` or ``/dev/ttyACM0`` — the number changes across
    reboots and re-enumerations, exactly like ``/dev/input/eventN`` does for
    touch (see docs/beta-finalization/touch/PIPELINE-TRACE.md);
  * exactly **one** host tool may own the port at a time (the console carries a
    kmsg mirror as well as a shell, so two readers steal each other's bytes);
  * every remote command is framed with a unique request id and verified by a
    target-side SHA-256, so a kernel-log line that shreds the stream can never
    be mistaken for a successful result;
  * **no write path may ever resolve onto a raw partition, a kernel/DTB/DTBO
    image, a bootloader interface or a modem/EFS/calibration region** — this
    module refuses such paths before a single byte leaves the host.

Nothing here talks to the network, writes to ``.qq``/RUN_ROOT, or flashes.
Stdlib only, so it runs on the plain macOS host Python.

Hard invariants enforced in code (not just in prose)
---------------------------------------------------
* ``assert_userspace_path()`` — every deploy target must live under an allowed
  userspace root and must not match a forbidden pattern (partition/boot/kernel/
  modem/EFS/PIT/calibration).
* ``FORBIDDEN_TOOLS`` — heimdall/odin/loki/pit tooling may never be invoked.
* ``RebootPolicy`` — refuses blind repeat reboots and refuses a reboot before
  the console has reconnected and userspace rollback is known-good.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import random
import re
import select
import subprocess
import sys
import termios
import time

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Device capability defaults.  These are the S10+ gadget's *advertised*
# capabilities (measured on the host with `ioreg -r -c AppleUSBACMData`), not a
# node name: any port that presents these capabilities is the right port.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
DEFAULT_VID = 0x18D1            # 6353  — Google Inc. (Android gadget VID)
DEFAULT_PID = 0x4EE7            # 20199 — Nuxel live-console gadget product id
DEFAULT_TTY_BASE = "usbmodem"   # CDC-ACM TTY base name
DEFAULT_SERIAL = "NUXEL-S10PLUS-0001"
DEFAULT_PRODUCT_RE = r"Nuxel.*(Live\s*)?Console"

#: Host serialisation lock (mirrors scripts/s10plus-debug-pack/nuxel-live.sh).
#: All tools use the same inode; an inaccessible lock fails closed.
LOCK_DIR = "/tmp"

#: Service units whose state is part of the A32 baseline snapshot.
BASELINE_UNITS = (
    "nuxel-wayland",
    "nuxel-wl-fb",
    "nuxel-button-manager",
    "nuxel-touch-arm",
    "seatd",
)

#: Paths whose contents prove which components own the display / animation.
BASELINE_FILES = (
    "/proc/cmdline",
    "/var/lib/nuxel/fb-owner",
    "/var/lib/nuxel/animation",
    "/run/nuxel-wl-fb.state",
    "/proc/bus/input/devices",
)

#: Kernel console byte budget per framed round trip (device N_TTY ring is 4 KiB
#: and the far end has no application-level flow control).
#: Longest framed shell line we transmit.  The far end is a Linux tty whose line
#: discipline buffer is 4096 bytes (N_TTY_BUF_SIZE); an over-long line is silently
#: truncated, which would corrupt a push.  Measured on the S10+ 2026-10-16: a
#: 4108-char wrapper round-trips with framed=True sha_ok=True, so the previous
#: 480-char ceiling was far too conservative — it refused every chunked push of a
#: path longer than ~120 chars (i.e. every /usr/share/nuxel/** target).  3800
#: leaves headroom under 4096 for the echoed prompt and the CR.
MAX_WRAPPER_LEN = 3800

#: `ioreg` decorates every registry line with a `|` tree glyph; tolerate it.
_PROP_RE = re.compile(r'[|\s]*"([^"]+)"\s*=\s*(.+)$')

KMSG_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*\d+,\d+,\d+,[-;c]")
KMSG_KEYS = ("SUBSYSTEM=", "DEVICE=", "ACTION=", "SEQNUM=", "DEVPATH=", "MAJOR=",
             "MINOR=", "DEVNAME=", "DEVTYPE=", "MODALIAS=", "TAGS=")


class ConsoleLost(RuntimeError):
    """The serial port died (unplug, gadget rebind, or the phone went away)."""


class SelectionError(RuntimeError):
    """No console node matched the required capabilities, or too many did."""


class GuardViolation(RuntimeError):
    """A live operation was about to touch something flash-adjacent."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Text helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def looks_kmsg(line: str) -> bool:
    """True for a line that is part of the target's live /dev/kmsg mirror."""
    if KMSG_LINE.match(line):
        return True
    s = line.strip()
    return any(s.startswith(k) for k in KMSG_KEYS)


def clean_lines(text: str) -> list:
    """Drop blank lines and kmsg-mirror noise from captured output."""
    return [l.rstrip() for l in text.splitlines() if l.strip() and not looks_kmsg(l)]

# Capability discovery  (macOS: ioreg; Linux host: /sys/class/tty)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def parse_ioreg_acm(text: str) -> list:
    """Parse `ioreg -r -c AppleUSBACMData -w0 -l` into capability records.

    Each record = {vid,pid,tty_base,tty_suffix,tty_device,callout,dialin}.
    The parser is deliberately tolerant: properties are read only inside the
    AppleUSBACMData block, and the IOSerialBSDClient child supplies the nodes.
    """
    nodes = []
    cur = None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if "<class AppleUSBACMData" in line:
            cur = {"vid": None, "pid": None, "tty_base": None, "tty_suffix": None,
                   "tty_device": None, "callout": None, "dialin": None}
            nodes.append(cur)
            continue
        if cur is None:
            continue
        m = _PROP_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        key, val = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip().strip('"')
        if key == "idVendor":
            cur["vid"] = _to_int(val)
        elif key == "idProduct":
            cur["pid"] = _to_int(val)
        elif key == "IOTTYBaseName":
            cur["tty_base"] = val
        elif key == "IOTTYSuffix":
            cur["tty_suffix"] = val
        elif key == "IOTTYDevice":
            cur["tty_device"] = val
        elif key == "IOCalloutDevice":
            cur["callout"] = val
        elif key == "IODialinDevice":
            cur["dialin"] = val
    return [n for n in nodes if n["callout"] or n["dialin"]]


def parse_ioreg_usb_devices(text: str) -> list:
    """Parse `ioreg -w0 -l -p IOUSB` into USB device capability records."""
    devs, cur = [], None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if "<class IOUSBHostDevice" in line:
            cur = {"vid": None, "pid": None, "serial": None, "product": None,
                   "node": line.split("+-o ", 1)[-1].split("  <")[0]}
            devs.append(cur)
            continue
        if cur is None:
            continue
        m = _PROP_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        key, val = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip().strip('"')
        if key == "idVendor":
            cur["vid"] = _to_int(val)
        elif key == "idProduct":
            cur["pid"] = _to_int(val)
        elif key in ("kUSBSerialNumberString", "USB Serial Number"):
            cur["serial"] = val
        elif key in ("kUSBProductString", "USB Product Name"):
            cur["product"] = val
    return devs


def _to_int(val: str, base=0):
    try:
        return int(val, base)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def enumerate_console_nodes(runner=subprocess.run) -> list:
    """Return live console capabilities actually present on this host.

    macOS  : ioreg capability lookup (no node-name assumption at all).
    Linux  : /sys/class/tty/*/device/../{idVendor,idProduct} capability lookup.
    """

                         capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20).stdout

            acm = ""
        nodes = parse_ioreg_acm(acm)
        for n in nodes:
            if not n.get("tty_device") and n.get("tty_base") and n.get("tty_suffix"):
                n["tty_device"] = "%s%s" % (n["tty_base"], n["tty_suffix"])
            if not n.get("callout") and n.get("tty_device"):
                n["callout"] = "/dev/cu.%s" % n["tty_device"]
            if not n.get("dialin") and n.get("tty_device"):
                n["dialin"] = "/dev/tty.%s" % n["tty_device"]

    nodes = []
    tty_root = "/sys/class/tty"

        entries = sorted(os.listdir(tty_root))

        return nodes

        sysdev = os.path.join(tty_root, name, "device")

            continue

        node = {"tty_device": name, "callout": "/dev/%s" % name,
                "dialin": "/dev/%s" % name, "tty_base": re.sub(r"\d+$", "", name),
                "tty_suffix": (re.search(r"(\d+)$", name) or [None, None])[1],
                "vid": None, "pid": None}
        walk = os.path.realpath(sysdev)
        for _ in range(6):
            walk = os.path.dirname(walk)
            vid_f, pid_f = os.path.join(walk, "idVendor"), os.path.join(walk, "idProduct")
            if os.path.exists(vid_f) and os.path.exists(pid_f):
                # sysfs reports idVendor/idProduct as bare HEX ("18d1"), not the
                # "0x18d1" ioreg prints on macOS.  int(val, 0) rejects a bare hex
                # string, which made this Linux branch find ZERO nodes on the S10+
                # host (measured 2026-10-16) even though the gadget was present.
                node["vid"] = _to_int(open(vid_f).read().strip(), 16)
                node["pid"] = _to_int(open(pid_f).read().strip(), 16)
                break
        if node["vid"] is not None:
            nodes.append(node)
    return nodes

--- test runner
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-all-tests.sh — the single offline/unit test entry point (briq-09a, area 52)
#
# WHAT THIS IS
#   One command that runs every *offline* test the Nuxel beta repository owns and
#   emits a machine-readable summary:
#
#     tools/beta/run-all-tests.sh                  # the release gate
#     tools/beta/run-all-tests.sh --list           # show the registry, run nothing
#     tools/beta/run-all-tests.sh --json -         # machine summary on stdout
#     tools/beta/run-all-tests.sh --only L1        # only suites whose id matches
#
#   Levels implemented (mission area 52):
#     L1  static checks          syntax (py/sh/JS), JSON validity, tree invariants
#     L2  unit / offline suites  per-group runners + validators + unit tests
#     L3  cross-component        the A32 baseline regression guard + the A33 suites
#     X   external (live/VM)     listed but NOT run here; unblocked with --external
#
# WHAT A GREEN RUN MEANS  (and what it does not)
#   Green here = the repository is internally consistent and every offline gate
#   passes.  It is OFFLINE_TESTED, nothing more.  It is NOT proof that the
#   handset boots, that the panel is right, that the touchscreen works, that
#   audio is audible, or that the firewall enforces anything on the phone.  Those
#   verdicts belong to the live/owner tiers and are recorded separately
#   (docs/beta-finalization/release/DEVICE-CAPABILITY-MANIFEST.json).
#
# THE TABLE (printed at the end of every run)
#   ID      suite id from the registry (also its log file name)
#   TIER    static | unit | cross | legacy | external
#   STATUS  PASS | FAIL | WARN | SKIP | EXTERNAL (listed, never run here)
#   CHECKS  how many PASS-shaped assertion lines the suite *printed*, counted by
#           count_checks() below.  A deliberate FLOOR, not a coverage claim: the
#           regex accepts "  PASS <name>", standalone ok/OK tokens and pytest's
#           "N passed" line.  A suite that prints nothing measurable reports "-"
#           and is never credited with assertions it did not print.
#   SECS    wall-clock seconds the suite took
#
# EXIT CODES
#   0  every hard suite passed (soft/legacy failures are reported as WARN)
#   1  at least one hard suite failed  == the release gate is RED
#   2  usage / environment error (no interpreter, unreadable registry)
#
# SAFETY (mission invariants, enforced by the L1-no-flash-invariants suite)
#   * never writes to a block device; never invokes heimdall/odin/fastboot/dd
#   * never writes under .qq/ or the QonQrete RUN_ROOT
#   * never writes a QonQrete receipt JSON into the workspace
#   * never starts/stops a service on the phone, never reboots, never flashes
#   * reports are written under build/reports/ (gitignored) only
#
# SCOPING NOTE (parallel build)
#   Eleven build groups write into this tree at the same time.  A suite whose
#   failure is caused by another group's *in-flight* work is listed in the
#   INFLIGHT_ALLOWANCES register below with its owning group, a reason, the
#   committed evidence log and an expiry date.  It is reported as WARN, loudly,
#   listed again in its own block at the end of the run, and preserved verbatim
#   in the machine-readable summary (`allowances_applied`,
#   `cross_group_failures`, `raw_gate`).  It is NEVER turned into a pass.
#
#   The register may only hold suites owned by ANOTHER group, and `--strict`
#   ignores it entirely and prints the raw release verdict.  The terminal
#   integration pass -- after every group has landed -- must be run with
#   --strict; that is the run whose gate is the release decision.
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
export ROOT

# ---- options -----------------------------------------------------------------
JSON_OUT=""
LOG_DIR=""
QUIET=0
STRICT=0
NO_STATIC=0
LIST_ONLY=0
ONLY_RE=""
EXTERNAL=0
TIMEOUT_SCALE=1

usage() { sed -n '2,50p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --json)     JSON_OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --log-dir)  LOG_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --only)     ONLY_RE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --timeout-scale) TIMEOUT_SCALE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --quiet|-q) QUIET=1; shift ;;
    --strict)   STRICT=1; shift ;;
    --no-static) NO_STATIC=1; shift ;;
    --external) EXTERNAL=1; shift ;;
    --list)     LIST_ONLY=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)  usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "run-all-tests: unknown option: $1" >&2; echo; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

REPORT_DIR="$ROOT/build/reports/beta-tests"
[ -n "$LOG_DIR" ] || LOG_DIR="$REPORT_DIR/logs"
[ -n "$JSON_OUT" ] || JSON_OUT="$REPORT_DIR/summary.json"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
LOG_DIR="$(cd "$LOG_DIR" && pwd)"
export LOG_DIR
case "$JSON_OUT" in
  /*|-) : ;;
  *) JSON_OUT="$ROOT/$JSON_OUT" ;;
esac

# `--json -` means "write the machine summary to stdout". Keep the real file in
# the report dir (so nothing is ever written to a file literally named "-") and
# stream it at the end.
if [ "$JSON_OUT" = "-" ]; then
  JSON_OUT_FILE="$REPORT_DIR/summary.json"
  SUMMARY_PATH="- (stdout; file: $JSON_OUT_FILE)"
  # Machine channel discipline: with `--json -` the JSON document is the ONLY
  # thing on stdout.  The human transcript (progress lines, results table,
  # allowance and failure blocks) is moved to stderr, so a caller can pipe stdout
  # straight into a JSON parser without stripping a table off the end.
  exec 9>&1
  exec 1>&2
else

        state = latest.get("state") or "pending"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# reboots anything or claims that any hardware works: live association,

#

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run-touch-tests.sh — the whole offline touch-pipeline test set, one command.
#
# Everything here runs on a workstation with NO phone, NO libinput, NO /dev/input
# and NO root.  It is the gate for build group "Priority 0 — Touchscreen &
# Reliable Interactive Input".  Nothing in this script writes to the phone, starts
# a service, arms an input node or reboots anything.
#
#   ./tools/s10plus/a33/tests/run-touch-tests.sh            # all tests
#   ./tools/s10plus/a33/tests/run-touch-tests.sh --quick     # skip the shim build
set -uo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
A33="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$A33/../../.." && pwd)"
QUICK=0
[ "${1:-}" = "--quick" ] && QUICK=1

rc_total=0
declare -a RESULTS=()

run_step() {   # run_step <name> <cmd...>
  local name="$1"; shift
  echo
  echo "==================== $name ===================="
  "$@"
  local rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" = 0 ]; then RESULTS+=("PASS  $name"); else RESULTS+=("FAIL  $name (rc=$rc)"); rc_total=1; fi
  return 0
}

echo "== Nuxel A33 touch-pipeline offline test set =="
echo "root: $ROOT"
echo "quick: $QUICK"

if [ "$QUICK" = 0 ]; then
  run_step "build the libinput shim (host selftest + aarch64 .so)" \
    "$A33/build-libinput-shim.sh" --selftest
fi
run_step "libinput shim: capability fixtures"      python3 "$HERE/test-libinput-path-fixture.py"
run_step "libinput shim: A31/A33 parity"           python3 "$HERE/test-libinput-parity.py"
run_step "libinput shim: the LD_PRELOAD invocation chain" python3 "$HERE/test-libinput-shim-invocation.py"
run_step "touch tracer: layers, gate, boundedness" python3 "$HERE/test-touch-trace.py"
run_step "MT frame parser: DOWN at SYN, tap != back, bottom swipe = home" \
  bash -c 'd=$(mktemp -d); trap "rm -rf \"$d\"" EXIT; cc -std=gnu11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-function -o "$d/test-touch-mt" "$1" && "$d/test-touch-mt"' _ "$HERE/test-touch-mt.c"
run_step "boot-mode guard: LPM detection + gates"  python3 "$HERE/test-bootmode-guard.py"
run_step "capture harness: commands, gate, no repo litter" python3 "$HERE/test-capture-harness.py"
run_step "no hard-coded /dev/input/event<N> gate"  python3 "$HERE/test-no-eventn-literal.py"

# OPTIONAL cross-check: the A32 baseline regression guard (owned by the preflight
# group).  Its result is reported verbatim and does NOT gate the touch test set,
# because another build group may be writing it concurrently.
echo
echo "==================== A32 baseline regression guard (optional) ===================="
if [ -x "$ROOT/tools/beta/regression-guard.sh" ]; then
  # --no-tests keeps this fast (hash-only); run it without it for the full gate.
  bash "$ROOT/tools/beta/regression-guard.sh" --no-tests
  echo "regression-guard rc=$?"
else
  echo "SKIP tools/beta/regression-guard.sh not present in this tree"
fi

echo
echo "==================== summary ===================="
for r in "${RESULTS[@]}"; do echo "$r"; done
if [ "$rc_total" = 0 ]; then
  echo "TOUCH-TESTS: ALL PASS"
else
  echo "TOUCH-TESTS: FAILURES PRESENT"
fi
exit "$rc_total"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Offline test entry point for Priority 4 (bg-04-userspace-completion).
#
# One command that re-derives every briq-04a/04b/04c acceptance claim from the
# repository alone:
#
#   briq-04a  docs/beta-finalization/system/DEPENDENCY-REPORT.md
#             images/s10plus/packages-manifest.json   (real Fedora 43 metadata)
#             tools/s10plus/a33/verify-packages.py
#   briq-04b  services/** + shell/config/systemd-user/**   (boot graph)
#             tools/s10plus/a33/verify-service-graph.py
#             services/nuxel-console/test-console-ownership.py (single-owner guard)
#   briq-04c  pwa/nuxel-common/**, services/nuxel-{bridge,portal,notifications,web}/**
#             services/nuxel-bridge/test-launcher-activation.py (registry -> launch)
#             services/nuxel-web (static PWA server)
#             tools/s10plus/a33/verify-app-registry.py
#
# Nothing here starts the phone, writes a partition, or touches .qq / RUN_ROOT.
# The result is OFFLINE_TESTED: a green run is NOT a claim that the handset boots
# (`systemctl is-system-running` belongs to the live-deployment group).
#
# Usage:
#   tools/s10plus/a33/tests/run-userspace-tests.sh            # everything
#   tools/s10plus/a33/tests/run-userspace-tests.sh --fast     # skip the network
#                                                             # metadata refresh
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)"
TESTS="$ROOT/tools/s10plus/a33/tests"
OUT="$ROOT/build/pkgmeta/userspace-test-results.json"
FAST=0
[ "${1:-}" = "--fast" ] && FAST=1

PASS=0; FAIL=0; SKIP=0
declare -a RESULTS=()

record() { # name, status, detail
  RESULTS+=("{\"name\": \"$1\", \"status\": \"$2\", \"detail\": \"$3\"}")
  case "$2" in
    PASS) PASS=$((PASS+1)); printf '  PASS  %s\n' "$1" ;;
    SKIP) SKIP=$((SKIP+1)); printf '  SKIP  %s (%s)\n' "$1" "$3" ;;
    *)    FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); printf '  FAIL  %s (%s)\n' "$1" "$3" ;;
  esac
}

/**
 * Nuxel common bridge — node-runnable test harness (ESM).
 *
 * Usage:
 *     cd pwa/nuxel-common && npm test
 *     node pwa/nuxel-common/test-bridge.js
 *
 * Starts a mock HTTP server that simulates the real nuxel-bridge endpoints
 * (/ping, /auth/token, /rpc) and exercises the shared bridge client
 * end-to-end: token bootstrap, token-header validation, generic RPC calls,
 * the window-token source, and mock fallback when the server is unreachable.
 */

import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import assert from 'node:assert';
import { NuxelBridgeClient, NUXEL_BRIDGE_VERSION, NuxelBridgeVersionError } from './bridge.js';

// The /ping response's bridge_version. undefined => the pinned value (healthy
// host); null => a legacy host that declares nothing; a string => a skewed host.
let VERSION_OVERRIDE;

// ---- Mock nuxel-bridge HTTP server --------------------------------
const authenticatedTokens = new Set();
const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
    const send = (code, body) => { res.statusCode = code; res.end(JSON.stringify(body)); };

    let body = '';
    req.on('data', (c) => (body += c));
    req.on('end', () => {
        let payload = {};
        try { payload = body ? JSON.parse(body) : {}; } catch (e) {}

        const path = req.url.split('?')[0];

        // Bootstrap: no auth required.
        if (path === '/api/v1/auth/token' && req.method === 'POST') {
            const token = 'sess-' + Date.now() + '-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
            authenticatedTokens.add(token);
            return send(200, { success: true, token, ttl: 3600, expires_at: Date.now() + 3600e3 });
        }

        // All other endpoints require a valid per-session token.
        const auth = req.headers.authorization || '';
        if (!auth.startsWith('Bearer ') || !authenticatedTokens.has(auth.slice(7))) {
            return send(401, { error: 'Unauthorized' });
        }

        if (path === '/api/v1/ping' && req.method === 'GET') {
            const proto = VERSION_OVERRIDE === undefined ? NUXEL_BRIDGE_VERSION : VERSION_OVERRIDE;
            const body = { status: 'ok', version: '0.5.2-beta' };
            if (proto !== null) body.bridge_version = proto;
            return send(200, body);
        }

        // Launcher -> app activation (briq-04c rev 2): the same shape the real
        // bridge returns, so the client contract (success / refusal) is exercised.
        if (path === '/api/v1/apps/activate' && req.method === 'POST') {
            const target = payload.target;
            if (target === 'org.nuxel.Mail') {
                return send(200, { success: true, id: target, type: 'pwa', action: 'navigate',
                                   url: '/pwa/nuxel-apps/mail/index.html', launchable: true,
                                   executed: false, source: 'registry', bridge_version: NUXEL_BRIDGE_VERSION });
            }
            if (target === 'org.nuxel.LiveConsole') {
                return send(200, { success: true, id: target, type: 'pwa', action: 'pending_app_tree',
                                   launchable: false, executed: false, owner_groups: ['bg-07-specialty-apps'],
                                   detail: 'the app tree is declared but not landed yet' });
            }
            if (target === 'nuxel-dialer') {
                return send(200, { success: true, id: target, type: 'native', action: 'exec',
                                   native_binary: '/usr/bin/nuxel-dialer', launchable: true, executed: false });
            }
            if (target === '../../bin/sh' || target === '/bin/sh') {
                return send(400, { success: false, error: 'invalid_app_id',
                                   detail: 'an app id is an identifier, never a path' });
            }
            return send(404, { success: false, error: 'unknown_app', app_id: target });
        }
        if (path === '/api/v1/apps/recent' && req.method === 'GET') {
            return send(200, { success: true, count: 1, max: 20, rejected: { count: 1, last: null },
                               activations: [{ id: 'org.nuxel.Mail', at: 1, action: 'navigate',
                                               requester: 'org.nuxel.Home', source: 'launcher' }] });
        }

        // Generic RPC.
        if (path === '/api/v1/rpc' && req.method === 'POST') {
            const { namespace, verb } = payload;
            if (namespace === 'storage' && verb === 'list-dir') {
                return send(200, { result: { success: true, entries: [{ name: 'readme.txt', path: '/readme.txt' }] } });
            }
            if (namespace === 'mail' && verb === 'imap-list') {
                return send(200, { result: { success: true, messages: [{ id: '1', subject: 'Hello' }] } });
            }
            if (namespace === 'camera' && verb === 'list-captures') {
                return send(200, { result: { success: true, captures: [] } });
            }
            return send(200, { result: { success: true } });
        }

        return send(404, { error: 'Not found' });
    });
});

let PORT;

"""Offline integration test: launcher -> bridge app activation (briq-04c).

The mission's application-infrastructure requirement is a *launcher-to-app
bridge*: the launcher resolves an app id to a launch descriptor through the
narrowly scoped privileged service, the one place app identity is decided, and
it must be impossible to turn that path into arbitrary execution.

This test runs the REAL HTTP bridge handler (services/nuxel-bridge/src/api.py)
against a real localhost socket, with inert `dbus` stubs - no D-Bus, no
hardware, no handset - and the REAL canonical registry

     native_binary; documented placeholder -> `launchable: false` + the
     registry's own note). Nothing in a descriptor is invented;
  2. a client-supplied `binary`, `command`, `url` or `path` NEVER changes the
     descriptor: the bridge reports the registry's values, so activation cannot
     be used to launch an arbitrary program;
  3. a path-shaped or unknown id is refused (`invalid_app_id` / `unknown_app`)

  4. an unavailable registry is a 503, never a fabricated app;
  5. activation is recorded in a BOUNDED history, observable through

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# regression-guard.sh — A32 baseline regression gate (briq-00d)
#
# The A32 build is the floor of the Nuxel beta finalization.  Eleven build groups
# are writing into this tree in parallel; this gate is what stops any of them (or
# a later cycle) from silently regressing what A32 proved on the handset:
#
#   INV-1  launcher/PWA cache invalidation (SW namespace bump + host purge + URL stamp)
#   INV-2  XRGB8888 -> DECON ABGR8888 colour conversion (source + real aarch64 selftest)
#   INV-3  ten-zone status-bar safe areas, S10+ portrait preset = zones 9,10
#   INV-4  hardware button manager as the single owner of gpio_keys
#   INV-5  live USB console keeps existing, staying executable and respawning
#   INV-6  userspace rollback route back to the known-working kiosk launcher
#   INV-7  the A32 release record itself stays byte-identical
#   INV-8  the NO-FLASHING / read-only-.qq / evidence-discipline register survives
#
# Behaviour is pinned hard; bytes are pinned hard only where this baseline owns the
# file exclusively (see docs/beta-finalization/BASELINE-PROTECTION.md section 2).
# An individual assertion may additionally declare "mode": "soft" in the register when
# the file it exercises is owned by another build group during the parallel run: a soft
# assertion that fails is reported as a WARN that names the owner, never as a FAIL and
# never as a silent pass.  Everything defaults to "hard".
#
# The same two-level rule governs FILE pins, and the precedence matters: a files[]
# entry may declare its own "hash_mode" (hard|soft|self) and THAT decides the verdict
# for that file.  The invariant-level "hash_mode" is only the DEFAULT for a file that
# declares none.  A soft file that drifts is therefore a WARN naming the owning group
# - never a FAIL - and the invariant's hard behavioural assertions (regex / json_eq /
# program / suite) still have to pass.  (Repaired by briq-02-gate-failure-repair: the
# guard used to OR the two modes, so INV-6's three bg-04-owned, explicitly soft
# shell/config/systemd-user/*.service pins failed the gate as "hard-pinned".)
#
#   regression-guard.sh                     full gate; exit 0 <=> nothing regressed
#   regression-guard.sh --quiet             print only the per-invariant summary line
#   regression-guard.sh --no-tests          skip the test-suite assertions (fast, hash-only);
#                                           soft assertions are skipped too and say so
#   regression-guard.sh --json              machine-readable result on stdout
#   regression-guard.sh --log PATH          override the log path
#   regression-guard.sh --repin PATH --reason TEXT
#                                           re-pin one protected file (the only sanctioned
#                                           way to move a hard pin; records old+new hash)
#   regression-guard.sh --help
#
# Exit codes: 0 = all enforced checks pass, 1 = at least one FAIL, 2 = usage/manifest error.
#
# SAFETY: this script never touches the phone, the framebuffer, the USB console or any
# block device.  It reads files, executes offline user-space tests, and for the colour
# leg runs the aarch64 bridge binary with --colour-selftest.

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
MANIFEST="$ROOT/docs/beta-finalization/baseline-protection.json"
# aarch64 ELFs cannot be executed on this macOS host; the UTM Fedora 43 guest is the
# documented execution channel (override with NUXEL_VM=user@host).
VM_HOST="${NUXEL_VM:-$(jq -r '.vm_host // "nuxel@192.168.64.3"' "$MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null || echo nuxel@192.168.64.3)}"

QUIET=0
JSON=0
RUN_TESTS=1
LOG_OVERRIDE=""
REPIN_PATH=""
REPIN_REASON=""

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --quiet|-q)   QUIET=1; shift ;;
    --json)       JSON=1; QUIET=1; shift ;;
    --no-tests)   RUN_TESTS=0; shift ;;
    --log)        LOG_OVERRIDE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --repin)      REPIN_PATH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --reason)     REPIN_REASON="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help)    sed -n '2,32p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "regression-guard: unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "regression-guard: jq is required (the register is JSON)" >&2
  exit 2
fi
if [ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]; then
  echo "regression-guard: manifest not found: $MANIFEST" >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! jq -e '.schema_version == 1 and (.invariants | type == "array")' "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "regression-guard: manifest failed to parse as a schema_version 1 register" >&2
  exit 2
fi

RUN_ID="$(date -u '+%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')"
if [ -n "$LOG_OVERRIDE" ]; then
  LOG="$LOG_OVERRIDE"
else
  LOG="$ROOT/build/out/beta/regression-guard-$RUN_ID.log"
fi
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")" 2>/dev/null || true
: > "$LOG" 2>/dev/null || true

N_PASS=0
N_FAIL=0
N_WARN=0
N_INFO=0
FAILED_IDS=""
WARNED_IDS=""

to_log() { [ -n "$LOG" ] && printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$LOG" 2>/dev/null; return 0; }
say()    { to_log "$*"; [ "$QUIET" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
raw()    { to_log "$*"; [ "$JSON" = "1" ] || printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
hdr()    { say ""; say "$*"; }

# ---- simple timeout wrapper (coreutils `timeout` when present) -----------------
with_timeout() { # with_timeout SECONDS cmd...
  local secs="$1"; shift
  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout "$secs" "$@"
  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gtimeout "$secs" "$@"
  else
    "$@"
  fi
}

# judge(): an assertion may declare "mode":"soft" in the register when the file it
# exercises is *owned by another build group* during this parallel run.  A soft
# assertion that fails becomes a WARN naming the owner instead of a FAIL, because the
# hard behavioural assertions for that invariant (regex/json_eq) are the actual gate.
# Default mode is "hard" and behaviour is unchanged for every other assertion.
judge() { # judge INVARIANT LABEL DETAIL   (uses $amode / $aowner)
  if [ "$amode" = "soft" ]; then
    record WARN "$1" "$2 (soft: ${aowner:-owned by another build group})" "$3"
  else
    record FAIL "$1" "$2" "$3"
  fi
}

sha_of() { # sha_of PATH -> hex or empty
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 1
  shasum -a 256 "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'
}

record() { # record STATUS INVARIANT LABEL [DETAIL]
  # DETAIL is optional: callers such as the manifest-consistency check pass 3 args.
  local st="$1" inv="$2" label="$3" detail="${4:-}"
  case "$st" in
    PASS) N_PASS=$((N_PASS + 1)); say "    PASS  $label${detail:+  [$detail]}" ;;
    FAIL) N_FAIL=$((N_FAIL + 1)); FAILED_IDS="$FAILED_IDS $inv"; say "    FAIL  $label${detail:+  [$detail]}" ;;
    WARN) N_WARN=$((N_WARN + 1)); WARNED_IDS="$WARNED_IDS $inv"; say "    WARN  $label${detail:+  [$detail]}" ;;
    INFO) N_INFO=$((N_INFO + 1)); say "    INFO  $label${detail:+  [$detail]}" ;;
  esac
  to_log "  -> $st $inv $label $detail"
}

# ---- --repin: the only sanctioned way to move a pin --------------------------
if [ -n "$REPIN_PATH" ]; then
  if [ -z "$REPIN_REASON" ]; then
    echo "regression-guard: --repin requires --reason '<why this byte changed>'" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  if [ ! -f "$ROOT/$REPIN_PATH" ]; then
    echo "regression-guard: --repin target does not exist: $REPIN_PATH" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  NEW_HASH="$(sha_of "$ROOT/$REPIN_PATH")"
  OLD_HASH="$(jq -r --arg p "$REPIN_PATH" '[.invariants[].files[] | select(.path == $p) | .sha256] | first // empty' "$MANIFEST")"
  if [ -z "$OLD_HASH" ]; then
    echo "regression-guard: '$REPIN_PATH' is not a registered protected asset with a pinned hash; nothing to re-pin." >&2
    echo "                  add it to docs/beta-finalization/baseline-protection.json first." >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  REPIN_AT="$(date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')"
  TMP_MANIFEST="$(mktemp -t baseline-protection.XXXXXX)"
  if jq --arg p "$REPIN_PATH" --arg h "$NEW_HASH" --arg old "$OLD_HASH" \
        --arg r "$REPIN_REASON" --arg at "$REPIN_AT" \
        '(.invariants[].files[] | select(.path == $p) | .sha256) = $h
         # A re-pin must move *every* byte expectation for that path, not just the
         # file pin: a type:"sha256" assertion carries its own copy of the expected
         # hash, and leaving it stale would make the register self-contradictory and
         # the very next guard run would fail on the file it just re-pinned.
         | ([.invariants[].assertions[]? | select(.type == "sha256" and .path == $p and .expect == $old)] | length) as $nsha
         | (.invariants[].assertions[]? | select(.type == "sha256" and .path == $p and .expect == $old) | .expect) = $h
         | .history += [{at: $at, event: "repin", path: $p,
                         old_sha256: $old, new_sha256: $h, reason: $r,
                         sha256_assertions_updated: $nsha}]' \
        "$MANIFEST" > "$TMP_MANIFEST"; then
    mv "$TMP_MANIFEST" "$MANIFEST"
    echo "regression-guard: re-pinned $REPIN_PATH"
    echo "  old sha256: ${OLD_HASH:-<none>}"
    echo "  new sha256: $NEW_HASH"
    echo "  reason:     $REPIN_REASON"
    echo "  assertions moved with the pin: $(jq -r '.history[-1].sha256_assertions_updated // 0' "$MANIFEST")"
    echo "  (recorded in the manifest history; the behavioural assertions for that"
    echo "   invariant still have to pass - a re-pin is a claim, not a proof)"
  else
    rm -f "$TMP_MANIFEST"
    echo "regression-guard: re-pin failed to update the manifest" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi

# ==============================================================================
# 0. Manifest-integrity and repository hygiene
# ==============================================================================
hdr "== regression-guard ==  manifest: docs/beta-finalization/baseline-protection.json"
say "   root:     $ROOT"
say "   run:      $RUN_ID"
say "   log:      $LOG"
say "   register generated: $(jq -r '.generated_at' "$MANIFEST")"
say "   baseline commit:    $(jq -r '.baseline.commit_a32' "$MANIFEST")"

HYG_FAIL=0
if [ "$(cd "$ROOT" 2>/dev/null && git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null)" != "true" ]; then
  record INFO HYGIENE "root is not inside a git work tree - ignore-rule check not applicable" "$ROOT"
else
for p in docs.zip scripts.zip tools.zip .venv; do
  if (cd "$ROOT" && git check-ignore -q "$p" 2>/dev/null); then
    :
  else
    record FAIL HYGIENE "repository hygiene: '$p' must stay gitignored (125 MB of supplied archives / 772-file virtualenv must never be committed)" "git check-ignore $p"
    HYG_FAIL=1
  fi
done
[ "$HYG_FAIL" = "1" ] || record PASS HYGIENE "repository hygiene: supplied archives and .venv stay gitignored" "docs.zip scripts.zip tools.zip .venv"
fi

# ---- manifest self-consistency: a sha256 assertion must agree with the file pin --
# A type:"sha256" assertion carries its own copy of the expected hash.  If it drifts
# away from the corresponding files[] pin the register contradicts itself (this is
# exactly the defect a --repin used to leave behind).  Detected here as a FAIL.
INCONS="$(jq -r '
  [.invariants[].files[] | select(.sha256 != null and .path != null)] as $files
  | [ .invariants[].assertions[]?
      | select(.type == "sha256" and .path != null and .expect != null)
      | .path as $ap | .expect as $ae
      | ($files | first(.[] | select(.path == $ap))) as $f
      | select($f != null and $f.sha256 != $ae)
      | "\($ap): assertion expects \($ae) but the file pin is \($f.sha256)"
    ] | .[]' "$MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null)"
if [ -n "$INCONS" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ -n "$line" ] && record FAIL MANIFEST-CONSISTENCY "register is self-contradictory: $line"
  done <<< "$INCONS"
else
  record PASS MANIFEST-CONSISTENCY "sha256 assertions agree with the file pins (a --repin moves both)"
fi

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Hash pins
# ==============================================================================
hdr "== 1. hash pins (hard = FAIL on drift, soft = WARN on drift) =="
HARD_TOTAL=0
HARD_OK=0
n_inv="$(jq '.invariants | length' "$MANIFEST")"
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt "$n_inv" ]; do
  inv_id="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].id" "$MANIFEST")"
  inv_title="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].title" "$MANIFEST")"
  inv_mode="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].hash_mode" "$MANIFEST")"
  n_files="$(jq ".invariants[$i].files | length" "$MANIFEST")"
  j=0
  while [ "$j" -lt "$n_files" ]; do
    fpath="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].files[$j].path" "$MANIFEST")"
    fexpect="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].files[$j].sha256 // empty" "$MANIFEST")"
    # A file pin may carry its own hash_mode.  The MODE PRECEDENCE is the rule the
    # register documents in BASELINE-PROTECTION.md section 2 ("soft | the file is
    # shared - another build group is contractually allowed to evolve it right now
    # | drift is a WARN") and section 10 rule 3: an explicit per-file mode WINS,
    # and the invariant-level mode is only the DEFAULT for a file that does not
    # declare one.  Before briq-02-gate-failure-repair the guard ORed the two, so a
    # file explicitly marked soft inside a hard invariant (INV-6's three
    # shell/config/systemd-user/*.service units, owned by bg-04) was reported as a
    # hard-pin FAIL - i.e. another group's announced mid-flight edit could turn the
    # gate red, which is exactly what the mode exists to prevent.
    fmode="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].files[$j].hash_mode // empty" "$MANIFEST")"
    frule="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].files[$j].role" "$MANIFEST")"
    fmode_eff="$fmode"
    [ -n "$fmode_eff" ] || fmode_eff="$inv_mode"        # invariant mode = the default
    if [ ! -e "$ROOT/$fpath" ]; then
      record FAIL "$inv_id" "protected file MISSING: $fpath" "$frule"
    elif [ "$fmode" = "self" ]; then
      record INFO "$inv_id" "self-referential pin skipped (the register cannot be pinned to its own hash): $fpath" "$frule"
    elif [ -z "$fexpect" ]; then
      record WARN "$inv_id" "no pinned hash recorded for $fpath" "$frule"
    else
      factual="$(sha_of "$ROOT/$fpath")"
      if [ "$factual" = "$fexpect" ]; then
        [ "$fmode_eff" = "hard" ] && { HARD_TOTAL=$((HARD_TOTAL + 1)); HARD_OK=$((HARD_OK + 1)); }
        say "    ok    $fpath  (${fmode_eff} pin held)"
        to_log "  -> pin $fpath $fmode_eff OK $factual"
      elif [ "$fmode_eff" = "hard" ]; then
        HARD_TOTAL=$((HARD_TOTAL + 1))
        record FAIL "$inv_id" "hard-pinned file changed: $fpath" "want $fexpect got $factual"
      else
        # soft: the bytes moved under a file another group owns.  A WARN, printed
        # loudly with the owning group named - never a pass, never a FAIL for
        # someone else's announced work.
        record WARN "$inv_id" "soft-pinned file drifted (shared with another build group): $fpath" \
          "was $fexpect now $factual (invariant owner: $(jq -r ".invariants[$i].owner_group // \"unstated\"" "$MANIFEST"))"
      fi
    fi
    j=$((j + 1))
  done
  i=$((i + 1))
done
if [ "$HARD_TOTAL" -gt 0 ]; then
  say "   hard pins: $HARD_OK/$HARD_TOTAL held"
fi

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Behavioural assertions from the register
# ==============================================================================
hdr "== 2. behavioural assertions =="
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt "$n_inv" ]; do
  inv_id="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].id" "$MANIFEST")"
  inv_title="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].title" "$MANIFEST")"
  say ""
  say "-- $inv_id : $inv_title"
  n_as="$(jq ".invariants[$i].assertions | length" "$MANIFEST")"
  j=0
  while [ "$j" -lt "$n_as" ]; do
    atype="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].type" "$MANIFEST")"
    alabel="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].label // .invariants[$i].assertions[$j].type" "$MANIFEST")"
    amode="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].mode // \"hard\"" "$MANIFEST")"
    aowner="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].owned_by // empty" "$MANIFEST")"
    case "$atype" in
      file_exists)
        apath="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].path" "$MANIFEST")"
        if [ -e "$ROOT/$apath" ]; then record PASS "$inv_id" "$alabel" "$apath"
        else judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "missing: $apath"; fi
        ;;
      file_executable)
        apath="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].path" "$MANIFEST")"
        if [ -x "$ROOT/$apath" ]; then record PASS "$inv_id" "$alabel" "$apath"
        else judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "not executable or missing: $apath"; fi
        ;;
      sha256)
        apath="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].path" "$MANIFEST")"
        awant="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].expect" "$MANIFEST")"
        amiss="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].on_missing // \"fail\"" "$MANIFEST")"
        if [ ! -f "$ROOT/$apath" ]; then
          case "$amiss" in
            warn) record WARN "$inv_id" "$alabel" "artefact absent: $apath (gitignored build output; rebuild with bash tools/s10plus/a32/build-a32.sh)" ;;
            info) record INFO "$inv_id" "$alabel" "artefact absent: $apath" ;;
            *)    judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "missing: $apath" ;;
          esac
        else
          agot="$(sha_of "$ROOT/$apath")"
          if [ "$agot" = "$awant" ]; then record PASS "$inv_id" "$alabel" "$agot"
          else judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "want $awant got $agot"; fi
        fi
        ;;
      regex)
        apath="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].path" "$MANIFEST")"
        apat="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].pattern" "$MANIFEST")"
        amin="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].min_count // 1" "$MANIFEST")"
        if [ ! -f "$ROOT/$apath" ]; then
          judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "missing: $apath"
        else
          acount="$(grep -Ec -- "$apat" "$ROOT/$apath" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          [ -n "$acount" ] || acount=0
          if [ "$acount" -ge "$amin" ]; then record PASS "$inv_id" "$alabel" "matches=$acount"
          else judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "pattern '$apat' matched $acount time(s), need >= $amin in $apath"; fi
        fi
        ;;
      json_eq)
        apath="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].path" "$MANIFEST")"
        apointer="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].pointer" "$MANIFEST")"
        awant="$(jq -c ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].expect" "$MANIFEST")"
        if [ ! -f "$ROOT/$apath" ]; then
          judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "missing: $apath"
        elif ! jq -e . "$ROOT/$apath" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "not valid JSON: $apath"
        else
          agot="$(jq -c "$apointer" "$ROOT/$apath" 2>/dev/null || echo '<none>')"
          if [ "$agot" = "$awant" ]; then record PASS "$inv_id" "$alabel" "$apointer = $agot"
          else judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "$apointer is $agot, want $awant"; fi
        fi
        ;;
      program)
        apath="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].path" "$MANIFEST")"
        amiss="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].on_missing // \"fail\"" "$MANIFEST")"
        an=$(jq ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].args | length" "$MANIFEST")
        aargs=""
        k=0
        while [ "$k" -lt "$an" ]; do
          aargs="$aargs $(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].args[$k]" "$MANIFEST")"
          k=$((k + 1))
        done
        awant_exit="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].expect_exit // 0" "$MANIFEST")"
        areq="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].require_stdout // empty" "$MANIFEST")"
        afor="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].forbid_stdout // empty" "$MANIFEST")"
        if [ ! -x "$ROOT/$apath" ]; then
          case "$amiss" in
            warn) record WARN "$inv_id" "$alabel" "binary absent or not executable: $apath (rebuild with bash tools/s10plus/a32/build-a32.sh)" ;;
            info) record INFO "$inv_id" "$alabel" "binary absent: $apath" ;;
            *)    judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "binary absent or not executable: $apath" ;;
          esac
        else
          afallback="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].exec_fallback // \"none\"" "$MANIFEST")"
          aout="$(cd "$ROOT" && with_timeout 120 "$ROOT/$apath" $aargs 2>&1)"
          aexit=$?
          awhere="host"
          # This host is macOS: it cannot exec an aarch64 Linux ELF ("exec format
          # error", rc=126).  When the register says exec_fallback=vm, the artefact is
          # deliberately run on the UTM Fedora 43 aarch64 guest instead - the same
          # escalation tools/s10plus/a32/tests/run-tests.sh performs.
          if [ "$afallback" = "vm" ] && { [ "$aexit" = "126" ] || printf '%s' "$aout" | grep -qi 'cannot execute binary file\|exec format error'; }; then
            awhere="$VM_HOST"
            avmout="$(with_timeout 60 scp -q -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=8 "$ROOT/$apath" "$VM_HOST:/tmp/a32-guard-$RUN_ID-$(basename "$apath")" 2>&1)"
            if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
              aout="$(with_timeout 120 ssh -q -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=8 "$VM_HOST" "chmod +x /tmp/a32-guard-$RUN_ID-$(basename "$apath") && /tmp/a32-guard-$RUN_ID-$(basename "$apath") $aargs; echo __RC=\$?" 2>&1)"
              aexit="$(printf '%s' "$aout" | sed -n 's/^__RC=//p' | tail -1)"
              aout="$(printf '%s' "$aout" | grep -v '^__RC=')"
              [ -n "$aexit" ] || aexit=255
            else
              aexit=255
              aout="scp to $VM_HOST failed: $avmout"
            fi
          fi
          aproblem=""
          if [ "$aexit" = "255" ] && [ "$awhere" != "host" ]; then
            record WARN "$inv_id" "$alabel" "aarch64 artefact cannot run here and $VM_HOST is unreachable (no aarch64 execution channel) - gate unavailable"
            to_log "$aout"
          else
            [ "$aexit" = "$awant_exit" ] || aproblem="exit=$aexit want=$awant_exit"
            if [ -n "$afor" ] && printf '%s' "$aout" | grep -q -- "$afor"; then aproblem="$aproblem; forbidden output '$afor'"; fi
            if [ -n "$areq" ] && ! printf '%s' "$aout" | grep -q -- "$areq"; then aproblem="$aproblem; required output '$areq' absent"; fi
            if [ -z "$aproblem" ]; then
              record PASS "$inv_id" "$alabel" "$(printf '%s' "$aout" | grep -c PASS) PASS line(s) on $awhere"
            else
              judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "$aproblem (ran on $awhere)"
              to_log "$aout"
            fi
          fi
        fi
        ;;
      suite)
        if [ "$RUN_TESTS" = "0" ]; then
          record INFO "$inv_id" "$alabel" "skipped (--no-tests)"
        else
          apath="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].path" "$MANIFEST")"
          ainterp="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].interpreter // \"bash\"" "$MANIFEST")"
          awant_exit="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].expect_exit // 0" "$MANIFEST")"
          areq="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].require_stdout // empty" "$MANIFEST")"
          aneed="$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].requires_build // empty" "$MANIFEST")"
          if ! command -v "$ainterp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            record WARN "$inv_id" "$alabel" "interpreter '$ainterp' absent - suite cannot run here"
          elif [ ! -f "$ROOT/$apath" ]; then
            judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "missing: $apath"
          elif [ -n "$aneed" ] && [ ! -e "$ROOT/$aneed" ]; then
            record WARN "$inv_id" "$alabel" "gate unavailable: $aneed not built (run: bash tools/s10plus/a32/build-a32.sh)"
          else
            aout="$(cd "$ROOT" && with_timeout 600 "$ainterp" "$ROOT/$apath" 2>&1)"
            aexit=$?
            if [ "$aexit" != "$awant_exit" ]; then
              judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "exit=$aexit want=$awant_exit: $(printf '%s' "$aout" | tail -3 | tr '\n' '|')"
              to_log "$aout"
            elif [ -n "$areq" ] && ! printf '%s' "$aout" | grep -q -- "$areq"; then
              judge "$inv_id" "$alabel" "required output '$areq' absent (exit=$aexit)"
              to_log "$aout"
            else
              record PASS "$inv_id" "$alabel" "exit=$aexit"
            fi
          fi
        fi
        ;;
      info)
        case "$(jq -r ".invariants[$i].assertions[$j].path // empty" "$MANIFEST")" in
          /dev)
            nodelist="$(ls /dev/cu.usbmodem* /dev/tty.usbmodem* 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
            if [ -n "$nodelist" ]; then
              record INFO "$inv_id" "$alabel" "console node(s) enumerated: $nodelist (reachability is an owner test, not a gate)"
            else
              record INFO "$inv_id" "$alabel" "no CDC-ACM console node enumerated right now"
            fi
            ;;
          *) record INFO "$inv_id" "$alabel" "" ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *)
        record WARN "$inv_id" "$alabel" "unknown assertion type '$atype' in the register"
        ;;
    esac
    j=$((j + 1))
  done
  i=$((i + 1))
done

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Summary
# ==============================================================================
hdr "== summary =="
say "   PASS=$N_PASS  FAIL=$N_FAIL  WARN=$N_WARN  INFO=$N_INFO"
if [ -n "$WARNED_IDS" ]; then
  say "   warned invariants:$WARNED_IDS"
  say "   (soft = a parallel build group changed a shared, protected file, or an assertion"
  say "    marked mode:soft could not be satisfied by the in-flight tree.  The hard behavioural"
  say "    assertions above are the actual gate; a soft signal is never a pass and never a"
  say "    baseline regression.)"
fi
if [ "$N_FAIL" -gt 0 ]; then
  raw "   REGRESSION GUARD: FAIL — failing invariants:$(printf ' %s' $FAILED_IDS | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"
  say "   A hard pin moves only via: tools/beta/regression-guard.sh --repin <path> --reason '<why>'"
  VERDICT="FAIL"
  RC=1
else
  raw "   REGRESSION GUARD: PASS — the A32 baseline is intact (no failing checks)."
  VERDICT="PASS"
  RC=0
fi
to_log "SUMMARY PASS=$N_PASS FAIL=$N_FAIL WARN=$N_WARN INFO=$N_INFO verdict=$VERDICT"

if [ "$JSON" = "1" ]; then
  printf '{"tool":"regression-guard","run":"%s","verdict":"%s","pass":%d,"fail":%d,"warn":%d,"info":%d,"failed_invariants":"%s","warned_invariants":"%s","log":"%s","baseline_commit":"%s"}\n' \
    "$RUN_ID" "$VERDICT" "$N_PASS" "$N_FAIL" "$N_WARN" "$N_INFO" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$FAILED_IDS" | tr -s ' ' ' ' | sed 's/^ //')" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$WARNED_IDS" | tr -s ' ' ' ' | sed 's/^ //')" \
    "$LOG" "$(jq -r '.baseline.commit_a32' "$MANIFEST")"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline test for the Nuxel application infrastructure (briq-04c).

Runs the REAL HTTP bridge handler (services/nuxel-bridge/src/api.py) against a
real localhost socket, with inert `dbus` stubs: no D-Bus, no hardware, no
handset. It proves the two contract-level properties the mission cares about:

  * the canonical app registry is served by the bridge, and an ABSENT registry
    is reported as unavailable instead of being replaced by an invented list;
  * the pinned bridge_version is published and a mismatching client is refused
    with an explicit 409 version_mismatch (never silently rejected).

Usage:  python3 tools/s10plus/a33/tests/test-app-infrastructure.py
"""

import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys
import threading
import types
import re
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import HTTPServer

ROOT = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "..", "..", ".."))
API_SRC = os.path.join(ROOT, "services", "nuxel-bridge", "src", "api.py")
REGISTRY = os.path.join(ROOT, "pwa", "nuxel-common", "app-registry.json")
PIN = os.path.join(ROOT, "pwa", "nuxel-common", "bridge-version.json")
BRIDGE_JS = os.path.join(ROOT, "pwa", "nuxel-common", "bridge.js")


def install_dbus_stub():
    """Minimal inert dbus so api.py imports; every bus call raises."""
    class _Raises:
        def __getattr__(self, name):
            def _boom(*a, **k):
                raise RuntimeError("no D-Bus in this test")
            return _boom

    dbus = types.ModuleType("dbus")
    dbus.exceptions = types.SimpleNamespace(DBusException=RuntimeError)
    dbus.Interface = lambda *a, **k: _Raises()
    dbus.SystemBus = lambda *a, **k: _Raises()
    dbus.SessionBus = lambda *a, **k: _Raises()
    mainloop = types.ModuleType("dbus.mainloop")
    glib = types.ModuleType("dbus.mainloop.glib")
    glib.DBusGMainLoop = lambda *a, **k: None
    mainloop.glib = glib
    dbus.mainloop = mainloop
    sys.modules["dbus"] = dbus
    sys.modules["dbus.mainloop"] = mainloop
    sys.modules["dbus.mainloop.glib"] = glib


def load_api(registry_path):
    install_dbus_stub()
    os.environ["NUXEL_HTTP_MODE"] = "dev"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("nuxel_api_under_test", API_SRC)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    mod.APP_REGISTRY_PATH = registry_path
    return mod


def main():
    failures = []

    def check(cond, msg):
        print(("  OK   " if cond else "  FAIL ") + msg)
        if not cond:
            failures.append(msg)

    pin = json.load(open(PIN))
    registry = json.load(open(REGISTRY))
    api = load_api(REGISTRY)
    api.BridgeAPIHandler.server_token = None

    server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), api.BridgeAPIHandler)
    port = server.server_address[1]
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % port

    def get(path, headers=None):
        req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, headers=headers or {})
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as res:
                return res.status, json.loads(res.read().decode())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            body = exc.read().decode()
            try:
                body = json.loads(body)
            except ValueError:
                pass
            return exc.code, body

    try:
        print("[infra] /api/v1/health publishes the pinned protocol version")
        status, body = get("/api/v1/health")
        check(status == 200, "health returns 200 (got %s)" % status)
        check(body.get("bridge_version") == pin["bridge_version"],
              "health bridge_version == pin %r (got %r)" % (pin["bridge_version"], body.get("bridge_version")))
        check(body.get("version") == pin["host_version"],
              "health version == host_version %r (got %r)" % (pin["host_version"], body.get("version")))
        check("registry" in body, "health reports the registry source")

        print("[infra] the bridge serves the canonical registry")
        status, body = get("/api/v1/apps/registry")
        check(status == 200, "registry endpoint returns 200 (got %s)" % status)
        check(body.get("available") is True, "registry is reported available")
        served = [a["id"] for a in body.get("apps", [])]
        expected = [a["id"] for a in registry["apps"]]
        check(served == expected, "served app ids == canonical registry ids (%d)" % len(expected))
        check(body.get("registry_version") == registry["registry_version"],
              "registry_version %r is served" % registry["registry_version"])
        check(body.get("bridge_version") == pin["bridge_version"],
              "the registry payload carries the pinned bridge_version")
        check("version_mismatch" not in body,
              "the served registry does not report a pin mismatch")

        print("[infra] an ABSENT registry is honest, not invented")
        api.APP_REGISTRY_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "does", "not", "exist.json")
        status, body = get("/api/v1/apps/registry")
        check(status == 200 and body.get("available") is False,
              "missing registry => available=false")
        check("apps" not in body, "missing registry => no fabricated apps[] list")
        check("not found" in (body.get("error") or ""), "missing registry => explicit error (%r)" % body.get("error"))
        api.APP_REGISTRY_PATH = REGISTRY
        print("[infra] a malformed registry is reported, not guessed")
        bad = os.path.join(ROOT, "build", "pkgmeta-test-bad-registry.json")
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(bad), exist_ok=True)
        with open(bad, "w") as fh:
            fh.write("{ this is not json")
        try:
            api.APP_REGISTRY_PATH = bad
            status, body = get("/api/v1/apps/registry")
            check(body.get("available") is False and "unreadable" in (body.get("error") or ""),
                  "malformed registry => available=false with an unreadable reason")
        finally:
            os.unlink(bad)
            api.APP_REGISTRY_PATH = REGISTRY

        print("[infra] the version gate refuses a mismatching client loudly")
        header = pin["http_header"]
        status, body = get("/api/v1/health", {header: pin["bridge_version"]})
        check(status == 200, "a client declaring the pinned version is served (200)")
        status, body = get("/api/v1/health", {header: "999"})
        check(status == 409, "a client declaring another version gets 409 (got %s)" % status)
        check(body.get("error") == "version_mismatch", "409 body names version_mismatch (%r)" % body.get("error"))
        check(body.get("expected") == pin["bridge_version"], "409 body names the expected version")
        check(body.get("got") == "999", "409 body echoes what the client declared")
        status, body = get("/api/v1/health")
        check(status == 200, "a legacy client without the header is still served (documented)")

        print("[infra] /api/v1/ping carries the protocol version")
        status, body = get("/api/v1/ping")
        check(status == 200, "ping returns 200 (got %s)" % status)
        check(isinstance(body, dict) and body.get("bridge_version") == pin["bridge_version"],
              "ping publishes bridge_version even when D-Bus is absent")

        print("[infra] the PWA client sends the pin and refuses a mismatch")
        js = open(BRIDGE_JS).read()
        check("options.headers['X-Nuxel-Bridge-Version'] = NUXEL_BRIDGE_VERSION" in js,
              "bridge.js sends the %s header" % header)
        check("export const NUXEL_BRIDGE_VERSION = '%s'" % pin["bridge_version"] in js,
              "bridge.js pins the protocol version to %r" % pin["bridge_version"])
        check("NuxelBridgeVersionError" in js, "bridge.js exposes a named version error")
        check("mockMode = true" in js, "bridge.js keeps an explicit mock mode for an unreachable host")

        print("[infra] D-Bus policies (configs/dbus is canonical)")
        dbus_dir = os.path.join(ROOT, "configs", "dbus")
        owners = {
            "org.nuxel.Bridge": ("root", None),
            "org.nuxel.Portal": ("root", "nuxel"),
            "org.nuxel.Notifications": ("root", None),
        }
        for name, (owner_user, owner_extra) in owners.items():
            conf = os.path.join(dbus_dir, "%s.conf" % name)

prereq_missing() {   # prereq_missing <need> -> prints reason, or nothing
  local need="$1" owner="$2" cmd="$3"
  case "$need" in
    ""|-) : ;;
    file:*)
      local f="${need#file:}"
      [ -e "$ROOT/$f" ] || { printf 'prerequisite file absent: %s' "$f"; return 0; }
      ;;
    probe:*)
      local probe="${need#probe:}"
      if ! ( cd "$ROOT" && eval "$probe" ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf 'host/artefact prerequisite unmet: %s' "$probe"
        return 0
      fi
      ;;
    *)
      command -v "$need" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'interpreter absent: %s' "$need"; return 0; }
      ;;
  esac
  # the command's first token may itself be a repo script that a parallel group
  # has not written yet (e.g. a new group runner)
  local first
  first="$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' | awk '{print $1}' | tr -d "'\"")"
  case "$first" in
    /*) : ;;
    *.sh|*.py|*.js|*.c)
      [ -e "$ROOT/$first" ] || { printf 'suite script absent: %s' "$first"; return 0; } ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Portable bounded execution (no coreutils `timeout` on the build hosts)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_bounded() {   # run_bounded <timeout-s> <logfile> <command>
  local tmo="$1" log="$2" cmd="$3"
  ( cd "$ROOT" && bash -c "$cmd" ) >"$log" 2>&1 &
  local pid=$!
  local waited=0
  local tick=2
  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
    if [ "$tmo" -gt 0 ] && [ "$waited" -ge "$tmo" ]; then
      kill -TERM "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      pkill -TERM -P "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 3
      if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        pkill -KILL -P "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        kill -KILL "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      fi
      wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      echo "TIMEOUT after ${tmo}s" >>"$log"
      return 124
    fi
    sleep "$tick"
    waited=$((waited + tick))
  done
  wait "$pid"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Suite selection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
selected_indexes() {
  local i=0
  while [ $i -lt ${#SUITE_ID[@]} ]; do
    if [ -n "$ONLY_RE" ]; then
      if ! printf '%s' "${SUITE_ID[$i]}" | grep -Eq "$ONLY_RE"; then i=$((i + 1)); continue; fi
    fi
    if [ "$NO_STATIC" -eq 1 ] && [ "${SUITE_TIER[$i]}" = "static" ]; then i=$((i + 1)); continue; fi
    printf '%s\n' "$i"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
}

# checked against the work queue.  A stale entry (its group has no unfinished
# record) is announced loudly and will NOT downgrade its suite.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
load_unfinished_groups
STALE_ALLOW=""
if [ ${#INFLIGHT_ALLOWANCES[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ "$QUIET" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo

  t0=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  run_bounded "$tmo" "$log" "$cmd"; rc=$?
  t1=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  dur=$((t1 - t0))

  CHECKS="$(count_checks "$log")"
  case "$CHECKS" in ''|0) CHECKS="-" ;; esac
  status="PASS"; note=""
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    status="PASS"; R_PASS=$((R_PASS + 1))
  elif [ "$rc" -eq 124 ]; then
    status="FAIL"; note="timeout after ${tmo}s"
  elif [ "$mode" = "soft" ]; then
    status="WARN"; note="soft suite failed (rc=$rc) — legacy, non-gating"
  elif allowance="$(allowance_for "$sid")" && allowance_is_live "${allowance%%|*}"; then
    status="WARN"; R_WARN_ALLOW=$((R_WARN_ALLOW + 1))
    note="IN-FLIGHT CROSS-GROUP ALLOWANCE (${allowance%%|*}): $(printf '%s' "$allowance" | cut -d'|' -f2) (rc=$rc)"
    ALLOW_HITS="${ALLOW_HITS}${sid}|${allowance}"$'\n'
  elif [ "$tier" = "external" ]; then
    status="EXT_BLOCKED"; note="external suite could not run (rc=$rc) — BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_RESOURCE"
  else
    status="FAIL"; note="rc=$rc"
  fi

  case "$status" in
    PASS) printf '  \033[32mPASS\033[0m %-30s %4ss  %6s checks\n' "$sid" "$dur" "$CHECKS" ;;
    WARN) R_WARN=$((R_WARN + 1)); printf '  \033[33mWARN\033[0m %-30s %4ss  %6s checks  %s\n' "$sid" "$dur" "$CHECKS" "$note" ;;
    EXT_BLOCKED) R_EXT=$((R_EXT + 1)); printf '  \033[36mBLK \033[0m %-30s %4ss  %6s checks  %s\n' "$sid" "$dur" "$CHECKS" "$note" ;;
    FAIL)
      R_FAIL=$((R_FAIL + 1)); [ -z "$FIRST_FAIL" ] && FIRST_FAIL="$sid"
      printf '  \033[31mFAIL\033[0m %-30s %4ss  %6s checks  %s\n' "$sid" "$dur" "$CHECKS" "$note"
      tail -8 "$log" | sed 's/^/        /' ;;
  esac
  if [ "$status" = "FAIL" ]; then
    FAIL_ROWS="${FAIL_ROWS}${sid}|${tier}|${owner}|${CHECKS}|${own_note:-$note}"$'\n'
  fi
  emit_row "$sid" "$tier" "$owner" "$status" "$rc" "$dur" "$CHECKS" "$mode" "$note" "$log"
done

T_END=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
T_TOTAL=$((T_END - T_START))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verdict + machine-readable summary
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The gate and the raw gate are different questions:
#   raw_gate  -> what a strict run (no cross-group allowances) would say
#   gate      -> the default run's verdict, which may have downgraded suites that
#                belong to another group that is still writing into this tree
if [ "$R_FAIL" -gt 0 ]; then GATE="red"; VERDICT="OFFLINE_TESTED_FAIL"; EXIT=1
    assert.strictEqual(recent.count, 1, 'the bounded activation history is observable');
    assert.strictEqual(recent.max, 20, 'the history is bounded');
    assert.strictEqual(recent.rejected.count, 1, 'refusals are counted for the Console view');
    console.log('[test] launcher -> bridge activation + activity history ok');

    // 5. Mock fallback when the server is unreachable.
    await new Promise((r) => server.close(r));
    const c3 = new NuxelBridgeClient({ apiUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:1', appId: 'org.nuxel.Offline' });
    const fallback = await c3.call('storage', 'list-dir', { path: '/offline' });
    assert.strictEqual(c3.mockMode, true, 'should fall back to mock mode');
    assert.strictEqual(fallback.success, true, 'mock fallback returns success');
    assert.strictEqual(fallback.mock, true, 'mock fallback flagged');
    console.log('[test] mock fallback ok');

    // 5. Pin integrity: the compiled-in literal is the protocol contract and the
    //    manifest helper agrees with it.
    assert.strictEqual(NUXEL_BRIDGE_VERSION, '1', 'pinned bridge_version');
    assert.deepStrictEqual(
        NuxelBridgeClient.checkManifest({ nuxel: { bridge_version: '1' } }),
        { compatible: true, declared: '1', expected: '1' });
    assert.strictEqual(
        NuxelBridgeClient.checkManifest({ nuxel: { bridge_version: '2' } }).compatible, false,
        'a manifest pinned to another protocol version is incompatible');
    assert.strictEqual(
        NuxelBridgeClient.checkManifest({}).compatible, false,
        'a manifest with no nuxel.bridge_version is incompatible');
    console.log('[test] bridge_version pin + manifest check ok');

    // 6. Version mismatch must be LOUD and must NOT degrade to mock data.
    //    Drop the window token from test 3 so each client bootstraps its own.
    delete globalThis.__NUXEL_TOKEN__;
    //    (a) host declares a different protocol version.
    await new Promise((r) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', r));
    PORT = server.address().port;
    VERSION_OVERRIDE = '999';
    const cVer = new NuxelBridgeClient({ apiUrl: base(), appId: 'org.nuxel.Skewed' });
    await cVer._init();
    assert.strictEqual(cVer.isConnected(), false, 'a skewed host is not a usable connection');
    assert.strictEqual(cVer.mockMode, false, 'a version mismatch must never enable mock mode');
    assert.deepStrictEqual(cVer.versionMismatch, { expected: '1', got: '999' });
    await assert.rejects(() => cVer.call('storage', 'list-dir', { path: '/' }), (e) => {
        assert.ok(e instanceof NuxelBridgeVersionError, 'thrown error is a NuxelBridgeVersionError');
        assert.strictEqual(e.code, 'NUXEL_BRIDGE_VERSION_MISMATCH');
        return true;
    });
    console.log('[test] version mismatch refused loudly (no mock fallback) ok');

    //    (b) a legacy host that declares nothing is also a mismatch.
    VERSION_OVERRIDE = null;
    const cLegacy = new NuxelBridgeClient({ apiUrl: base(), appId: 'org.nuxel.Legacy' });
    await cLegacy._init();
    assert.strictEqual(cLegacy.mockMode, false, 'legacy host must not silently enable mock mode');
    assert.deepStrictEqual(cLegacy.versionMismatch, { expected: '1', got: null });
    console.log('[test] undeclared host version refused loudly ok');

    //    (c) the healthy host is accepted, and the pin is exposed.
    VERSION_OVERRIDE = undefined;
    const cOk = new NuxelBridgeClient({ apiUrl: base(), appId: 'org.nuxel.Ok' });
    await cOk._init();
    assert.strictEqual(cOk.isConnected(), true);
    assert.strictEqual(cOk.getBridgeVersion(), NUXEL_BRIDGE_VERSION);
    console.log('[test] healthy host accepted ok');

    await new Promise((r) => server.close(r));

    console.log('\n[test] ALL TESTS PASSED');
    process.exit(0);
}

main().catch((e) => {
    console.error('[test] FAILED:', e);
    process.exit(1);
});
